stem: A nurse notices that an electrical medical device has a frayed power cord. What is the appropriate action?

options.A: Finish the current treatment with the device before reporting the frayed cord because removal from service can wait until care is complete.
options.B: Remove the damaged device from service and send it through the organization’s qualified inspection, repair, and safety-testing process before reuse.
options.C: Cover the frayed section with adhesive tape and return the device to routine use if the equipment continues to function normally.
options.D: Repair the cord at the bedside when no bare conductor is visible because clinical staff may correct minor electrical defects during use.

rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(2)(ii) requires defective or damaged cord-and-plug-connected equipment that might expose an employee to injury to be removed from service. No employee may use it until repairs and tests necessary to render the equipment safe have been made. Therefore B is correct.
educational_objective: Remove electrical equipment with a potentially hazardous damaged cord from service until qualified repair and safety testing have made it safe for reuse.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(2)(i) Visual inspection for external defects including damage to outer jacket/insulation; §1910.334(a)(2)(ii): damaged item that might expose an employee to injury must be removed from service and may not be used until repairs and tests render it safe.
source_claim_supported: Electrical equipment with a frayed/damaged cord that may expose personnel to injury must be removed from service until repaired and tested safe.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_original.stem: A nurse notices that an electrical medical device has a frayed power cord. What is the appropriate action?

options.A: Finish the current treatment with the device before reporting the frayed cord because removal from service can wait until care is complete.
options.B: Remove the damaged device from service and send it through the organization’s qualified inspection, repair, or replacement process before reuse.
options.C: Cover the frayed section with adhesive tape and return the device to routine use if the equipment continues to function normally.
options.D: Repair the cord at the bedside when no bare conductor is visible because clinical staff may correct minor electrical defects during use.

source_original.rationale: OSHA requires defective or damaged electrical equipment that may expose employees to injury to be removed from service until repaired and tested as safe.
source_original.source_detail: 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(2)(ii), Visual inspection — defective/damaged equipment removed from service until repaired and tested. eCFR/OSHA standard currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: infection prevention, biohazard handling, security plans, equipment safety and workplace safety. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the electrical-safety construct and key B, tightened the action to OSHA's exact remove-repair-test sequence, and preserved easy difficulty because the final item tests a direct safety standard.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item directly reflects the regulatory remove-from-service requirement and does not authorize bedside improvised repair.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because potentially hazardous damaged equipment must be removed from service rather than used to finish treatment.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because tape/continued function does not satisfy required repair and safety testing.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the standard requires safe repair/testing before reuse, not ad hoc bedside correction during use.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B follows the regulatory sequence.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are actions the nurse might take after identifying the frayed cord; B is uniquely compliant.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — equipment and workplace safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read OSHA §1910.334(a)(2), hospital electrical-safety summary, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. B remained uniquely correct.
